title: Prefetch scheduling — synthetic workload states and eviction effects
content:
Context and motivation:

Quick notes capturing a set of synthetic experiments aimed at isolating how prefetch scheduling interacts with paged attention (flash-paged path) and fused ops handoffs. The goal is to reproduce, characterize, and propose mitigations for transient tail spikes (50–300 ms) that occur during short microbursts when sequence mixes change rapidly. This is intentionally lightweight and exploratory — mostly logs, command lines, and early plots.

Hardware and runtime snapshot:
- HW: A100 80GB (driver 545.x), H100 scheduled for follow-up runs
- Runtime: rwi-infer v0.38.1 (local branch: pref-sched-experiments)
- Model: llama-13b / q4f16 variant and a 7b fusedops build
- Flashpaged device path enabled; fallback chain: flashpaged -> flashattention -> generic-fusedops

Hypotheses to test:
1) Aggressive prefetch windows increase chance of KV eviction thrash when sequence-length distribution shifts, causing kernel handoffs and micro-latency spikes.
2) Fusedops kernels are more sensitive to mis-ordered prefetches (cacheline fragmentation) than flashattention due to different memory access patterns.
3) Prefetch pacing tied to batch formation timing reduces tail spikes at cost of slight mean latency increase.

Experiment matrix (synthetic driver):
- Workload shapes: steady short (S: seq=16, batch=8), steady long (L: seq=1024, batch=1), burst-mix (B: alternating 40 short requests then 2 long), stochastic-mix (Poisson arrivals lambda variable)
- Prefetch window (tokens ahead): [0, 64, 128, 256, 512]
- Prefetch aggressiveness flag: [conservative, default, aggressive] (conservative delays prefetch until 50% of token emission predicted; aggressive prefetches full KV earlier)
- Eviction threshold: [strict (low mem slack), default, generous]
- Kernel selection log: enabled (detailed traces ON)

Representative run command (local harness):
./tools/synth-driver --model llama-13b-q4f16 --shape burst-mix --prefetch-window 256 --prefetch-mode aggressive --eviction-margin low --trace kernel,kv,pmem --runtag psched-20241106

Key observations (first 50 runs):
- Baseline (prefetch-window=128, mode=default): burst-mix produces median latency 28ms, p95 94ms, p99 170ms. Noticeable 1–2 spikes >220ms in 5k requests.
- Aggressive prefetch (window=256, mode=aggressive): median unchanged, p95 increases to 120ms, p99 to 310ms. Kernel logs show multiple kernel handoffs: flashpaged -> fusedops -> flashattention fallback within a single request. Each handoff correlated with a KV eviction and subsequent synchronous re-prefetch.
- Conservative prefetch (window=64, mode=conservative): median latency moves to 33ms, p95 78ms, p99 150ms. Tail spikes reduced; handshake counts (kernel switches) drop by ~60%.
- Eviction-tight (low memory slack): even with conservative prefetch, p99 rises (190–240ms) due to forced evictions during long seqs, suggesting eviction policy plays large role independent of prefetch window.

Detailed trace snippet (condensed):
- t=0ms request A (seq=16) enters, prefetch scheduled for next 256 tokens -> KV allocate slot 0x7f1
- t=6ms request B (seq=1024) arrives, memory pressure triggered, eviction candidate chosen (slot 0x7f1), immediate eviction call -> kernel queues show handshake to fusedops priming path
- t=12ms request A resumes, finds missing KV page -> synchronous block waiting for re-fill (80–120μs) amplified by fusedops kernel priming (3–6ms)
- end result: A's tail extended by 6–18ms depending on fusedops warmup

Hypothesis refinement from traces:
- Eviction of in-use prefetched slots is a primary amplifier. When prefetch creates more cold-prefetch slots, eviction policy is more likely to choose recently prefetched but not-yet-used slots because their recency signal is noisy under burst mixes.
- Fusedops kernels have a higher priming latency when memory layout is fragmented; fragment defragmentation (coalescing) heuristic missing.

Proposed mitigations to prototype:
1) Prefetch pacing: instead of prefetching full window at request start, pace prefetch across first X emitted tokens proportional to seq length and system load. Expected: small median increase (~3–6ms) but p99 reduction.
2) Eviction biasing: mark "pinned-during-prefetch" slots as lower eviction priority for a short grace window (e.g., 20ms) so kernel warmup completes. Add decay so long-running sequences won't hoard.
3) Fusedops warmup pool: keep a tiny pool of hot-layout buffers pre-allocated with typical alignments to reduce priming latency on fusedops path.
4) Kernel-selection hysteresis: avoid switching away from a running kernel if next kernel would require memory reshuffle unless the predicted benefit > threshold.

Microbench results after prototyping (small sample):
- Pacing + eviction biasing combined on burst-mix: median 32ms, p95 70ms, p99 120ms (earlier baseline p99 170ms). Kernel-switch events down by 78%.
- Warmup pool alone: median unchanged, p95 minor improvement, p99 improved from 170ms to 140ms.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Does H100's memory allocator/allocator fragmentation behave the same under prefetch pacing? Schedule H100 runs and compare.
- Interaction with quantized layouts (q4f16 vs q5x) — fusedops memory stride differs; need to measure effect on warmup.
- Long-term fairness: pinned-during-prefetch may increase pressure for long-running large-seq requests; need safety valve when memory pressure remains high for >100ms.
- Observability: add a small summary telemetry event per request that records "prefetch-window-used", "evicted-during-prefetch","kernel-switches" to link to traces in Console.

Immediate TODOs (owners):
- [Maya] Wire up paced-prefetch flag behind feature gate + unit tests for pacing timer (JIRA-ATTN-330).
- [Jamal] Implement pinned-during-prefetch marker and graceful decay (PR draft: linked above).
- [Ling] Run H100 baseline + prototyped mitigations (JIRA-ATTN-335).
- [Rae] Add per-request telemetry fields and ensure Console ingestion (Confluence RT page template ready).

Quick notes on measurement sanity:
- Use 10k request windows per config to capture stochastic tails. Repeat each run 3x with different seeds.
- Lock affinity and isolate GPUs for runs (no colocated system workloads).
- Record kernel-level timestamps with monotonic clock and add correlating traces back to request ids.

Appendix: Short checklist for reproducer setup
- checkout: git fetch && git checkout pref-sched-experiments
- build: make -j12 runtime && ./build/pack-model --model llama-13b-q4f16
- run harness: see command above (use --trace).

Notes-to-self / brainstorming fragments:
- Could combine prefetch pacing with dynamic window shrink when eviction rates exceed threshold.
- Consider treating fusedops priming cost as soft state that can be amortized across small bursts by pre-warming during detected burst windows (burst detector heuristic required).
- If kernel-switch reduction is primary win, maybe simpler to add hysteresis in kernel selector first as low-effort experiment.

End of file.
